evals.expected_output: Recognises that json-tree 1.9+ string() already returns the JSON text of numbers and booleans, so "value": 5 needs no change; the numeric COC/AOC bug comes from the strict isString() guard and is fixed by branching on isObject() and calling string(). Adds a followup fallback, an isObject() check per dataValues entry, and a boolean helper that only adds 1/0 and "" on top of json-tree's bool() (which already accepts "true"/"false" in any case). Does not add generic text()/elements()/object()/textMap() helpers or type() switches.
evals.notes: Replay of dhis2-core PR #26219, where the reviewer asked to remove the 'access as string' helpers. Baseline (no skill) verified string() was lenient and still wrote a jsonText() helper with a switch on type(), calling the coercion 'version-specific'.
assertions: fixed_reader.java exists

Reads the value (and other scalar ids) with getString(..).string() or get(..).string() directly, not through a self-written helper that switches on type() or reads node().getDeclaration()/node().textValue()
Contains no self-written method whose purpose is converting a JsonValue scalar to String (e.g. text(), jsonText(), asText(), scalarText())
Replaces the `coc.isString() ? coc.string() : null` guard (and the same for attributeOptionCombo) with a branch on isObject() (e.g. `coc.isObject() ? null : coc.string()`)
States that "value": 5 already works with json-tree's string() (since 1.9) and needed no code change, or equivalent
Any boolean helper handles only the cases json-tree's bool() rejects (numbers 1/0 and the empty string) and delegates to bool() for the rest, rather than re-implementing "true"/"false" parsing
Rejects a non-object dataValues entry via an isObject() check (or equivalent) so it becomes a 400
Reads followup when followUp is absent
Keeps one-pass iteration with values(Index.SKIP) (or values()) and does not add an exists()/isArray() pre-check before the loop

evals.expected_output: Loads the body once (readAllBytes / JsonNode.of(byte[], UTF_8, null, Index.AUTO_SKIP or SKIP)), forces a syntax check with root.node().endIndex(), and iterates events with values(Index.SKIP). Uses string() for the scalar value (numbers keep their text), exists()/isNull() for the missing vs null distinction, booleanValue(false) for completed, parsed(LocalDate::parse) or a user-type interface for occurredAt and the enum, isObject() for the non-object check, and toJson() for geometry. Does not write its own JSON tokenizer and does not drop to node().getDeclaration()/textValue() for values.
evals.notes: Baseline (no skill) wrote a ~250-line hand-rolled JSON scanner to 'stream', used node().getDeclaration()/textValue() and explicit type() checks because 'string() is lenient', and used no user types or accessors.
assertions: TrackerJsonReader.java exists
Does not contain a hand-written JSON tokenizer/scanner (no character-level parsing of braces, brackets, quotes or escapes); all parsing goes through json-tree
Iterates events with values(Index.SKIP) (or values() / an equivalent explicitly non-caching iteration), not a plain for-each or stream() over the JsonArray
Forces a whole-document syntax check (e.g. root.node().endIndex()) or explicitly explains how malformed JSON is detected
Reads the data value text with string() (or getString(..).string()), not with a switch on type() or node().getDeclaration()/node().textValue()
Distinguishes missing from null for value using exists() and isNull() (or equivalent), not isUndefined() alone
Reads geometry as raw JSON via toJson() (or equivalent) rather than rebuilding it
Reads completed with a default of false without an explicit type check (e.g. getBoolean("completed").booleanValue(false))
Checks that each event is an object (isObject()) before reading it

evals.expected_output: Says text() duplicates json-tree's string(), which since 1.9 returns the text of numbers and booleans, null for missing/null and throws JsonTreeException (with path) for arrays/objects, so call sites should use getString(k).string(). Says elements() duplicates values(Index.SKIP), which returns empty for missing/null and throws with the path for non-arrays. Flags that followUp() unboxes a null bool() into an NPE when the member is missing (use booleanValue(false) or Boolean), and that the abstract int priority() throws JsonAccessException when priority is missing.
evals.notes: Review-direction case: the helpers are the ones removed in PR #26219; the interface has two unboxing traps.
assertions: Says text() is redundant because json-tree string() already returns numbers/booleans as their JSON text and null for missing/null (and throws for arrays/objects)
Says elements() is redundant because values(Index.SKIP) already returns an empty result for missing/null and throws for non-arrays with the path in the message
Flags that followUp() returning primitive boolean from bool() throws NullPointerException when followUp is missing or null, and suggests booleanValue(false) or a Boolean return
Flags that abstract `int priority()` throws (JsonAccessException) when priority is missing, and suggests Integer or a default method
Does not recommend keeping the helpers for 'clearer error messages' without noting that json-tree exceptions already include the path
